checks_run.procedure: Judge D-234's open questions. D-229: connector configuration names stay cannot-name. D-228 (4): cross-organization ids are out of scope. Look for a served column, response, notification channel or write path that still names a sensitive record, or a token sequence that loses or misplaces a hidden literal after edits, grant changes or concurrent saves. Also look for a way to disclose the new 0127 key or the tag.
checks_run.command: git diff cde60365..33db1a46 (all 22 product files); grep for restricted_token_key, SCHEMA_COLUMNS consumers, selectAll() readers of automation_rule_version, audit record() calls in versions.ts/lifecycle.ts/rules.ts, DB roles in deploy/compose/db-init; probes of QA-R11-07/08/10
checks_run.expected: No served path names a sensitive record; no token sequence loses or misplaces a literal; the key is never served.
checks_run.actual: Nothing between round 10 and this candidate touches connectors or the sensitive-reference sweeps (the diff is automation-only). My round-10 judgement stands. D-229: field_mappings sources and credential_refs are typed by people who already see that configuration; they are not served references to records, so they stay cannot-name. D-228 (4): the D-218 id-refs sweep on the demo stack finds no restricted id in either language or locale, so the ruling holds. Key and tag: every audit event writes an explicit changes map (create: automation_rule_id, version_no, based_on_version_id, content_sha256; update: CONTENT_COLUMNS only; publish/supersede/discard: status). The serializer builds content from named columns only (contentOfRow). The only SCHEMA_COLUMNS consumer is the catalogue test. The DB has only mth_owner and mth_app. P18 finds the key in no response, header, audit row or outbox payload. The tag is HMAC-SHA256 over a domain string, the row id and the row version, truncated to 96 bits. Without the key it cannot be computed or checked, and P18 finds no id fragment in it.
